reason: Resolved the three local findings without changing any original Statement or Definition, so no consumer interface repairs were triggered. Prepared for the required final whole-batch review. The 2026 claimed uniqueness result remains an unverified open-problem source, not a logical supplier.

findings.reason: Added lem-ip-anisotropic-conductivity-map-wellposedness to justified_by; that lemma already depends on this Definition, so the well-definedness edge introduces no cycle.

Added the uniqueness argument that makes the weak solution linear in the first boundary datum, and the representative argument that makes the energy pairing linear in the second. Together with the existing bound, this proves bounded bilinearity.
Extended the weak-gradient chain rule and energy change-of-variables identity from smooth approximants to all H1 classes, and used that identity in the weak-solution and DN-map steps.

The 2018 survey describes the general nonanalytic anisotropic problem with full or local data as open [Daudé–Kamran–Nicoleau, §1](https://arxiv.org/html/1803.00910v1). I retrieved and read all 43 pages of the primary 2026 preprint, whose Theorem 1.1 claims this same-patch result [preprint PDF](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/preprints/Smooth-Anisotropic-Uniqueness-in-the-Calderon-Problem-from-One-Boundary-Patch-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), but did not independently validate the continuation arguments in §§3.3–3.5 or the moving-sphere estimates in §§4–5. In §7.1, Proposition 7.2 also asserts that the original interior equals the extended interior minus the open cap; this appears false on the glued patch P0, which is interior to the extension but boundary in the original manifold. The preservation conclusion appears recoverable from the whole-manifold complement. The item status now records this uncertainty and keeps the claim unverified.
